Cool Old Lady: She's sweet and has a sense of humor, gently ribbing Ethan while she visits Juliet. Meaningful Name: Her name is one of severalshout outsthe show makes toAmelia Earhart.

characters.name: Widmore
characters.description: A wealthy industrialist and the father of Penelope Widmore and Daniel Faraday. He had a long-running rivalry with his successor as leader Benjamin Linus over control of the Island, though rules limited their ability to attack one another. Arch-Enemy: Ben and Desmond's. His conflict with Desmond eventually resolved itself, with Widmore acknowledging that Desmond made his daughter happy and was a good man (although neither Desmond nor Penny knew this or forgave him). His rivalry with Ben was much more long-lasting and on equal footing. Arc Villain: Pretty much only the main antagonist of Season 4. Season 5 he’s around much less and by Season 6 he’s actively working with the heroes in anEnemy Minesituation. The Atoner: In Season 6, when he returns to the island under Jacob's behest. It seems that the death of Daniel and his daughter's estrangement has made him realize how much his quest for power has cost him. Widmore is hardly a good guy, but he's at least trying to defeat the Man in Black. Bad Boss: He has little hesitation in sending his underlings off to die. Averted with his attempt at redemption in Season 6, when he's saddened by the deaths of those under his charge.

characters.name: Zoe
characters.description: A geophysicist hired by Charles Widmore to lead his team on the Island. Asshole Victim: Zoe was smug and arrogant, so it's hard to care much when the Man in Black slits her throat. Character Death: The Man in Black slashes her throat. Death by Irony: When confronted by Ben and the Man in Black, Widmore tells her not to talk in order to keep her alive. By telling her to stay silent, this makes her useless to the Man, who slits her throat in response. The Dragon: The last of Charles Widmore's dragons, following somewhat successful runs from Keamy and Abaddon. By the time he got around to Zoe, the application process had clearly gotten less picky.

characters.name: Seamus
characters.description: A scientist who worked for Charles Widmore in 2007. He was brought to the Island as part of a support team. Asshole Victim: Borders onCruel and Unusual Deathas well. When the Man in Black attacks Widmore's team at the Hydra in his smoke form, he flings Seamus into the air and smashes him so hard against one of the cages, it kills him instantly and leaves imprints of the bars on his face. Jerkass: From what we see, Seamus is short-tempered and argumentative. Red Shirt: He exists mostly to be killed by the Man in Black and make it seem like Widmore didn't just bring Zoe and a group of nameless peons.

characters.name: Abaddon
characters.description: An agent of Charles Widmore, whose job was to get people to "where they needed to be". Affably Evil: Much more "affable" than "evil", from what we see. He's initially very pleasant to Hurley and he treats Locke with genuine sympathy. Ambiguously Evil: He works for Charles Widmore. That's pretty much the only bad thing about him that we know of: Ben says he's an extremely dangerous man, but Ben is unreliable. Bald of Evil: He's bald, but onlyAmbiguously Evil. Character Death: Abaddon is shot to death by Ben.

characters.name: Bakir
characters.description: An assassin for Charles Widmore. Bald of Evil: He's an absent-haired assassin. Character Death: Bakir is shot several times in the back by Sayid. In the Back: Sayid shoots him in the back, while Bakir is distracted by Ben. Karmic Death: Killed by his victim's husband.

characters.name: Peter Avellino
characters.description: A wealthy Italian man. Affably Evil: Avellino is a very genial and jovial man with a good sense of humour. Character Death: Sayid kills him on a golf course. Corrupt Corporate Executive: He's an extremely wealthy man and works for Widmore. Offstage Villainy: His crimes are unclear, but he does work for Widmore.

characters.name: Ivan Andropov
characters.description: A Russian man allegedly working for Charles Widmore who was assassinated by Sayid Jarrah. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: When Sayid confronts him, he frantically begs for his life. Character Death: He's assassinated by Sayid. Offstage Villainy: It's unclear what he did, but working for Charles Widmore usually means you're not a saint.

characters.name: Elsa
characters.description: A girlfriend of Sayid, she is in fact revealed to be a spy working for an unnamed "economist" and trying to kill Sayid and his boss Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Elsa appears to be a sweet, thoughtful woman but in reality she'sThe Mole, and a ruthless one at that. Character Death: She's killed by Sayid. Dark Action Girl: For the Widmore Corporation. Femme Fatale: She manages to get in with Sayid by romancing him.

characters.name: Gault
characters.description: The captain of the freighter Kahana sent by Widmore to find the island and Benjamin Linus. He is originally seen as antagonistic and untrustworthy, but he later becomes an ally of Desmond and Sayid, allowing them the freighter's zodiac boat to ferry castaways from the island to the freighter after he becomes concerned at the lengths Keamy is willing to go to secure Ben. Bad Boss: Subverted; he's first seen beating the snot out of a crewman who tried to visit the Island out of boredom, but given theharmful effectseven being near the Island are causing several of Gault's crew, effects made worse by getting closer to the Island, his actions are closer to tough love than any kind of cruelty. When the time comes to stand up to Keamy, Gault doesn't hesitate to draw a gun in defense of his crew. Badass Longcoat: Wears a long sweeping coat. Character Death: When Gault tries to stop Keamy from going to the island to carry out his mission, the crazed mercenary pulls a gun and shoots him in the heart. Gault dies instantly. The Good Captain: Of the Kahana. He turns out to be a decent man, as opposed to an untrustworthy villain like many assumed he would be.

characters.name: Minkowski
characters.description: The communications officer aboard Widmore's freighter. Though he at first obstructs the survivors' attempts to contact the outside world, he later assists Desmond in calling Penny. He ultimately dies of temporal displacement on the boat. He later appears in the Sideways world as Desmond's driver, where he gives him the Oceanic 815 manifest. Butt-Monkey: In his physical appearance, he becomes sick and gets restrained. He keeps going through his horrible time displacement illness before finally dying. Character Death: Minkowski is unfortunately unable to find his constant, and dies from temporal displacement. Deadly Nosebleed: A symptom of his temporal displacement. Deadpan Snarker: He even makes jokes about his ownSanity Slippage.

characters.name: Ray
characters.description: A physician who served aboard the freighter Kahana. Asshole Victim: Of Keamy. He was such a jerk that he isn't mourned much. Bald of Evil: Although he isn't so much evil as callous and lazy. Character Death: Keamy cuts his throat and tosses him overboard, mostly to prove a point to Frank. Doomed by Canon: One of the oddest uses of this trope ever made; due to theTimey-Wimey Ballsurrounding the Island, we see his dead body days before we see what killed him, so for most of his appearances it's clear that he's a dead man walking.

characters.name: Regina
characters.description: A crew member aboard the Kahana. Character Death: Suffering from cabin fever, Regina covers herself in chains and jumps into the ocean. Driven to Suicide: By her cabin fever. She weighs herself down with chains and jumps into the sea. Mauve Shirt: She exists mostly to show how badly circumstances on the freighter have deteriorated. Sanity Slippage: As part of the cabin fever brought on by the island, she started to go crazy. Frank caught her reading a book upside-down.

characters.name: Naomi
characters.description: Recruited by Matthew Abaddon and employed by Charles Widmore, Naomi is the leader of the group on a mission to capture Ben Linus and remove him from the island. She is the first to arrive on the island and tells the Oceanic survivors of the freighter Kahana. While she claims she is there to rescue Desmond Hume, her true mission is later revealed. Naomi dies of her wounds after Locke throws a knife into her back. Action Girl: She was able to climb a tree while dying from a knife wound, and leaps from the tree to get the drop on Kate.Dark Action Girl: According to Ben, although we never see her do anything truly evil aside from working for Widmore while having knowledge of his tendency to murder people. Dark Action Girl: According to Ben, although we never see her do anything truly evil aside from working for Widmore while having knowledge of his tendency to murder people. Ambiguously Evil: She was hired by then-Big BadCharles Widmore, lied about the nature of her mission to the survivors, andBenclaims that she's extremely dangerous, but Naomi also seemingly helps the survivors with no obvious ill intent, and she doesn't seem to be affiliated with the definitely malicious Keamy beyond their mutual employer. Whether or not Naomi was genuinely well-intentioned is an answer that she takes to her grave. Character Death: Locke knifes Naomi in the back. She survives for a few hours afterwards, even managing to get a warning out to the freighter, but then dies from her injuries.

characters.name: Keamy
characters.description: The lead mercenary on the Kahana and a former Marine. Keamy leads a team onto the island to find Ben, killing Karl and Danielle Rousseau and later executing Alex in front of Ben. Keamy eventually tracks Ben down and is stabbed to death by him. His death causes the freighter to explode via a fail-deadly switch which monitors his heartbeat. All Devouring Black Hole Loan Sharks: In the flash-sideways. Arc Villain: Though Widmore hired him and so he's technically following his boss's orders, Keamy himself is the main antagonist of season 4. Though he starts out by mainly antagonizing Ben, once his forces get crushed by the Monster, Keamy ultimately becomes such a threat to everyone on the Island that the survivors and the Others have to team up to stop him. Ax-Crazy: Keamy becomes increasingly unhinged as he goes back and forth between the island and the freighter. Gault suggests he's suffering from the same cabin fever that affected Regina and Minkowski. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He seems perfectly pleasant when he's first introduced.That is not the case.

characters.name: Omar
characters.description: One of the mercenaries sent by Charles Widmore to the Island aboard the freighter Kahana. All Devouring Black Hole Loan Sharks: In the flash-sideways. Bald of Evil: His head is shaved bald. Beard of Evil: In the flash-sideways. Character Death: When a grenade lands near him, Keamy kicks it away. It lands at Omar's feet, blowing him up.

characters.name: Horace
characters.description: A mathematician who served as the compassionate but ineffectual leader of the Dharma Initiative during their years on the island. Alcohol-Induced Idiocy: Following a fight with Amy, Horace gets drunk and starts setting off dynamite early in the morning. Dies Wide Open: Horace dies with his eyes open after being gassed during the Purge. Ben closes his eyes as a sign of respect. Drowning My Sorrows: After finding out that Amy kept her ex-husband Paul's ankh pendant, he argues with her and gets drunk as a result. Extreme Doormat: Horace lets everyone walk right over him, especially Radzinsky.

characters.name: Radzinsky
characters.description: A member of the DHARMA Initiative who worked at the Flame station in 1977 as Head of Research, enjoying a relatively high leadership position within the Initiative. Arc Villain: Radzinsky is the main villain of the Dharma Initiative arc during season 5. Ate His Gun: How he died. There's a stain on the ceiling of the Swan Station marking the spot where he did it. Bald of Evil: He's bald on top with longer hair around the side of his head. Beard of Evil: He has a full beard.

characters.name: Phil
characters.description: A member of the DHARMA Initiative who worked in security under the authority of James "Sawyer" Ford, who was using the alias of "Mister"LaFleur. Big Ol' Eyebrows: They're...very prominent. Bound and Gagged: By Sawyer after he comes to him about the video evidence. Character Death: During the incident, flying magnetic poles shoot right through him. The Dragon: To Radzinsky, eventually.

characters.name: Amy
characters.description: A member of the DHARMA Initiative on the Island in the 1970s and was the first member of the Initiative to meet the time travelling survivors. She was the wife of Horace Goodspeed and the mother of Ethan Rom. Character Death:Word of Godis that she died in the Purge. Happily Married: To Paul, and later has a not-entirely-happy marriage with Horace. Mama Bear: For Ethan. Lady Macbeth: In her few appearances, she proved to bemuchmore bloodthirsty than her husband.

characters.name: Lara Chang
characters.description: Pierre Chang's wife and the mother of Miles Straume. She was a member of the DHARMA Initiative and lived on the Island in the 1970s. Character Death: Lara dies of cancer prior to the series. Posthumous Character: She's long dead of cancer by the time the series starts. The Topic of Cancer: It isn't said explicitly, but it certainly looks like she's dying of cancer when Miles visits her.

characters.name: Roger
characters.description: The father of Benjamin Linus, whom he regularly abused, both verbally and possibly physically, and berated as a child. He was employed as a DHARMA Initiative "Workman," and his uniform featured the Swan station logo. Abusive Parent: To Ben, who he abuses verbally and physically. The Alcoholic: After finding out he's to be a janitor for the Dharma Initiative, he begins drinking heavily. Alcoholic Parent: Ben often comes home to find him passed out in an alcoholic stupor. Asshole Victim: While he does show a slightly more likeable side right before his death, he was still an abusive, self-pitying jerk, so it's hard to feel sympathetic when Ben gasses him to death.

characters.name: Kelvin
characters.description: A member of the U.S. Army and later the DHARMA Initiative. He manned the Swan station after his arrival on the island, originally with his partner Stuart Radzinsky, by himself for a time, and later with Desmond. Death by Falling Over: When Desmond tackles him, Kelvin hits his head on some rocks and dies. Drowning My Sorrows: Inman deals with his sense of hopelessness by getting drunk in the Station. Jaded Washout: By the time Desmond meets Kelvin, he's become a disillusioned and bitter man. Jerkass: He's pretty condescending and gets irritated when Desmond questions him.

characters.name: Annie
characters.description: Ben's childhood friend on the Island. Aborted Arc: Along with Alex, Darlton said that Annie was one of the two most significant women in Ben's life. They even said, "Annie is going to prove to be very significant in Ben's life" but she's never seen again. Michael Emerson, Ben's actor, expressed some disappointment they never returned to Annie's story. Childhood Friends: With Ben in the Dharma Initiative. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She was meant to be very important to Ben's story, but disappears entirely after a single episode. She was apparently evacuated with all the other Dharma children in 1977 and didn't return. Only Friend: To a young Ben, who wasn't exactly the most out-going of kids. Annie was the only person to befriend him.

characters.name: Oldham
characters.description: A chemist and DHARMA Initiative member who performed interrogations. The Aloner: Lives all the way on the outskirts, completely in isolation from the rest of the Dharma Initiative. Cold-Blooded Torture: Oldham is given a good bit of build-up, so it's expected, but he uses a chemical mixture instead of physical torture. Traumatic, sure, but nothing compared to what Sayid's done. Creepy Monotone: Never raises his voice. The Dreaded: Sawyer is very wary of taking Sayid to him, referring to him as a psychopath.

characters.name: Danielle
characters.description: A woman of French origin who was shipwrecked on the Island with an expedition in 1988, seven months pregnant with her daughter, Alex. Shortly after Danielle gave birth, her daughter was taken away by Benjamin Linus, an Other. Rousseau lived alone for sixteen years, and over time became slightly disturbed due to her isolation. Action Girl: 16 years on the island has made her handy with a gun. The Aloner: Even after the Survivors prove themselves to be allies, Danielle prefers to live alone in the jungle. Aloof Ally: She's firmly on the survivors' side, but it's largely based more on their mutual hatred for the Others, and she doesn't tend to actively help them out unless it helps her own interests as well. Annoying Arrows: As Ben found out when she shoots him through the back.

characters.name: Robert
characters.description: A member of Danielle Rousseau's science expedition that became shipwrecked on the Island. Robert was Alex's biological father and was Danielle's lover. Brainwashed and Crazy: By the Smoke Monster. Character Death: After he's brainwashed by the Smoke Monster, Danielle is forced to kill him. She gave him every chance, but he pulled the trigger on her only find she'd removed the firing pin. Knowing that the Robert she knew was lost, Danielle shot him. Disappeared Dad: To Alex as Danielle had to kill him shortly before giving birth. Dwindling Party: Part of Rousseau's team that quickly diminishes thanks to the Monster.

characters.name: Montand
characters.description: A member of Danielle Rousseau's science expedition. Ambiguous Situation: Moments after Montand has his arm ripped off, his voice calls out to the team asking for their help. However, 19 years later, his skeleton is found more or less at the same opening in the Temple wall that he was dragged into, suggesting he died almost immediately. It's possible that the voice was actually the Man in Black and that Montand was already dead by this point. How long the Man in Black would have impersonated him for is unclear, but it's possible his team didn't realise he was dead until much later, as Rousseau later recounts this event as the day Montand lost his arm, which would be an odd way to describe it if he died the same day. An Arm and a Leg: His arm is ripped off by the Smoke Monster. Asshole Victim: The Monster kills him, but he was such a dick it's hard to give a shit. Character Death: The Monster dragged him into the ground, ripping his arm off in the process. He was either killed by the shock, blood loss or was just finished off once the Monster had him underground.

characters.name: Nadine
characters.description: One of the members of the science expedition that arrived on the Island on a life raft in a storm in 1988. Character Death: She disappears while on the island, and is likely to have been killed by the Monster. Dwindling Party: Part of Rousseau's team that quickly diminishes thanks to the Monster. Killed Offscreen: Nadine disappears suddenly, presumably killed by the Monster. Posthumous Character: Only seen in flashbacks, having died 16 years prior to the main timeline.

characters.name: Brennan
characters.description: A member of Danielle Rousseau's science expedition, which was marooned on the Island in 1988. Character Death: After he was 'infected' Danielle shot him. Brainwashed and Crazy: By the Monster, according to Danielle. Dwindling Party: Part of Rousseau's team that quickly diminishes thanks to the Monster. The Ghost: Right up until Season 5. He was mentioned in Danielle's transmission right back in the Pilot, but didn't actually make a physical appearance until Season 5 when Jin travelled back in time.

characters.name: Margo
characters.description: Jack's mother and Christian's widow. Outliving One's Offspring: Margo was alive in her last appearance, and is presumably still alive after Jack returns to the Island and dies saving it. Satellite Character: She doesn't have much character herself, existing pretty much just to facilitate plot between Jack and Christian. Small Role, Big Impact: It's Margo who insists that Jack go to Australia to retrieve Christian, the thing that put him on Flight 815. Widow's Weeds: She dons a wide-brimmed hat with a veil for Christian's memorial service.

characters.name: Diane
characters.description: The mother of Kate Austen. All Girls Want Bad Boys: She loves and adores her abusive drunk of a husband more than her own daughter. She even divorced the decent and upstanding Sam Austen to go back to Wayne. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She seems like a typical battered housewife and sweet waitress; the reality is that she placed her alcoholic, abusive husband before her own flesh and blood. She never forgives Kate for killing Wayne, taking every opportunity (save one) to turn her into the police. She even tries to threaten Kate with her testimony in exchange for seeing her "grandson". Domestic Abuse: Diane's husband Wayne would beat her when he was drunk (which was often). Entitled Bitch: After Kate returns from the Island with Aaron, Diane believes, despite choosing the loathsome Wayne over her own daughter and trying to turn Kate over to law enforcement, that she deserves a chance to meet who she believes to be her grandson, even being willing to threaten Kate over it.

characters.name: Carmen
characters.description: Hurley's mother. She is a devout Catholic, and is fluent in Spanish. She is often overbearing towards Hurley. Abusive Parents: She just not smothering, but also hits his son often for trivial reasons. Christianity Is Catholic: She's very devoutly Catholic. She even gets a golden Jesus (and she hilariously puts her hands over Jesus' ears when talking about sex with her husband). Deadpan Snarker: She earned some degree of adoration by fans due to the sheer hilarity of her lines. Dirty Old Woman: Carmen admits (after covering the ears on a statue of Jesus) that part of why she brought David back into her and Hurley's lives is because she "has needs".Hurley is not pleased to hear about it.

characters.name: David
characters.description: Hurley's father, and husband of Carmen Reyes. The Atoner: For abandoning his son. After he returns, David gradually realizes what a mistake it was to abandon his family and dedicates himself to being a better father to Hurley. Cool Old Guy: It's Cheech Marin! Of course he's cool! Deadpan Snarker: As is the standard for any character played by Cheech Marin. Dirty Old Man: Much to Hurley's horror, David remarks with approval that Carmen is "a passionate woman".

characters.name: Nadia
characters.description: Nadia Jaseem is the long lost love of Sayid Jarrah. The two were childhood friends in Iraq and she became involved in the insurgency against Saddam Hussein. Sayid, who was an interrogator for the Republican Guard, was assigned to interrogate her and instead helped her escape. Sayid's priority in life is to find his way back to Nadia, and he was headed to Los Angeles to find her when the plane crashed. Agony of the Feet: The soles of her feet were flayed during her captivity. Broken Bird: Subverted. Despite all the horrible things she goes through, Nadia doesn't let it get to her and stays a cheerful, good-hearted woman. Character Death: While out with Sayid, she's hit by a car as she's crossing the street. She dies shortly after in Sayid's arms. Childhood Friend Romance: With Sayid. As children, Nadia would push him in the mud and tease him so that he would notice her. They eventually get married as adults.

characters.name: Cooper
characters.description: John Locke's biological father. Cooper was shown to have used the alias of Adam Seward, and he claimed to have used Tom Sawyer, TedMacLaren, Louis Jackson and Paul, among others. He was, by his own admission, a con man. As "Tom Sawyer", he seduced James Ford's mother, Mary Ford and then used her in order to swindle money from her and her husband, which resulted in the death of both. This prompted James to take on the alias "Sawyer", and to hunt down his namesake. Abusive Parents: Very much so. Aside from the implications of either abusive or disinterested foster parents, Locke's own father frequently ruins his life with no remorse and ultimately tries to kill his own son. Archnemesis Dad: To Locke. He abandons him, steals his kidney, abandons him again, destroys Locke's romantic relationship with Helen (albeit not on purpose) and eventually tries to kill him. Asshole Victim: Go on, it's okay to admit you cheered when Sawyer strangled him with a chain. It's to the point that even Locke, his own son, outrightthanksSawyer for doing it. Billy Needs an Organ: He shows the true depth of his sociopathy when he pretends to reconcile with his son so he can convince him to donate his kidney, thenabandon him after the operation.

characters.name: Mrs Dawson
characters.description: Michael's mother and Walt's grandmother. Mama Bear: Toward Walt, of whom she's very protective. Never Mess with Granny: She's capable of giving Michael a very stern talking to and does the same to Hurley when Walt goes to meet with him. Outliving One's Offspring: Michael is killed when the Freighter explodes in the Season 4 finale, leaving his mother to raise the now orphaned Walt. Promotion to Parent: After Michael's return and later death, she raises Walt. Interestingly, this is exactly what Michael suggested in a panic after Susan died.

characters.name: Mr. Paik
characters.description: The CEO of the South Korean corporation Paik Heavy Industries. Mr. Paik was Sun's father and Jin's father-in-law, as well as Jin's employer. Archnemesis Dad: Eventually, he becomes this to Sun. By the time she returns from the Island, she's grown to hate her father for the malign influence he exerted over the lives of her and Jin. Corrupt Corporate Executive: He's an extremely rich and extremely corrupt man, whose company either exists as a front for his regular business of blackmail and murder, or is kept alive by it. The Corrupter: To Jin. The Don: Of his criminal empire.

characters.name: Carole
characters.description: Claire's mother, Lindsey's sister, Christian Shephard's former lover and Aaron's grandmother. Convenient Coma: A car accident puts her into a coma for years on end. She only comes out of it after the plane crash. Outliving One's Offspring: Carolebelievesthat Claire died in the crash of Flight 815, but is eventually informed by Katethat Claire is alive. Red Herring: Jack and Kate initially believe that Carole hired Dan Norton to try and take Aaron away from Kate. After Jack confronts her about it, however, it becomes clear that Carole doesn't even know who Aaron is and her hiring Norton was a complete coincidence (she retained his services as part of a lawsuit against Oceanic Airlines over Claire's presumed death). It's later revealed that Ben hired Norton as part of his plan to get the Oceanic 6 back on the Island.

characters.name: Randy
characters.description: The cruel, diabolical, and taunting middle management boss for whom both Hurley and Locke have worked. Bad Boss: He's mean-spirited, bullying and cruel to his employees. Beard of Evil: When he's working in Locke's office, although he's later seen without it. The Bully: To Locke especially, who he detests for some strange reason that may have something to do with Locke being in a wheelchair. Control Freak: He looks into Locke's personnel file and takes things off his desk.

characters.name: Cassidy
characters.description: A divorcée who fell in love with Sawyer, but was conned by him, and later gave birth to his daughter Clementine. She also became friends with Kate. All Girls Want Bad Boys: She falls in love with Sawyer, even when she knows he's a con man. Con Woman: When Sawyer's con (seemingly) fails, she asks him to teach her how to con people. She learns from Sawyer and works with him for a time before they split and she goes solo. Law of Inverse Fertility: She's understandably mixed about discovering that in addition to conning her, Sawyer also impregnated her. One Degree of Separation: She knew Sawyer and Kate before they ended up on the island together.

characters.name: Dr Brooks
characters.description: Hurley's therapist at the Santa Rosa Mental Health Institute. During his sessions with Hurley, he focused on helping Hurley feel better about himself, and he helped Hurley examine his unhealthy relationship with food. Nice Guy: A genuinely caring doctor who only wants to help his patients. He does everything he can to help Hurley better himself. Not So Above It All: He's generally a competent and well-intentioned guy, but he does accept a bribe from Hurley in the flash-sideways. It's in the form of a donation to the hospital, however, and not a donation to his own pocket.

characters.name: Leonard Simms
characters.description: A former U.S. naval officer who Hurley knew at Santa Rosa Mental Health Institute. Madness Mantra:"4...8...15...16...23...42..." Sanity Slippage: He was driven insane by the numbers. Talking to Themself: Leonard only repeats the numbers to himself over and over.

characters.name: Dan Norton
characters.description: An attorney working for the Agostini & Norton law firm, and Benjamin Linus's lawyer. Amoral Attorney: Norton doesn't do anything really illegal, but has no qualms harassing Kate so she'll be pushed into returning to the Island. Punch-Clock Villain: He's only doing a job for Ben. Smug Smiler: Always seen with a big grin on his satisfied face.

characters.name: Big Mike
characters.description: A police officer, and later detective, for the LAPD and the partner of Ana Lucia Cortez before she quit the force. All Love Is Unrequited: Implied for Ana Lucia. He tries to get information out of Hurley about her and describes her as 'gorgeous' in a melancholy tone. Hidden Heart of Gold: He acts like a hard-ass to intimidate Hurley, but he's actually a good-natured fellow and an excellent cop. Reasonable Authority Figure: Despite hiding hisHidden Heart of Gold, he actually treats Hurley pretty well for someone who'd led the police on a car chase. When he was a beat cop with Ana Lucia, he was even-tempered and kept a leash on herHot-Bloodedways.

characters.name: Karen Decker
characters.description: A public relations representative of Oceanic Airlines. The Cameo: For Science Fiction mainstay, Michelle Forbes. Miss Exposition: She's the one who describes the false circumstances of the Oceanic Six's 'rescue'.

characters.name: Malkin
characters.description: A self-professed psychic in Australia whom Claire visited several times while pregnant with Aaron. Con Man: Malkin pretends to be a fortune teller to con people out of money. He's rather good at it, too. Fortune Teller: Subverted, it's all a charade. Irony: Malkin makes his living as aPhony Psychic, and his daughtermay well have hadagenuinesupernatural experience. Manipulative Bastard: Successfully manipulates Claire through careful lies and actions. Malkin first gives Claire her money back, pretending he 'saw' something terrible, and then slowly pushed her into boarding the plane.

characters.name: Bram
characters.description: A member of a team that worked for or with Jacob. He abducted Miles shortly before the departure of the Kahana, and offered him an alternative to joining Widmore's team. He directly opposed Widmore and had interests in the Island, claiming that he was on "the winning side" of the war. He was also a passenger aboard Ajira Airways Flight 316 and a survivor of the crash on the Hydra Island. The Big Guy: In Ilana's group. He's the one who leads the charge against the Man in Black. Character Death: Bram shoots at the Man in Black, who reacts violently. While the Man in Black (in his smoke form) kills his friends, Bram places ash around himself to protect him. The Man in Black pulls down some stone pillars, knocking Bram out of the protective circle. Then he grabs him, lifts him up and impales him on a splint of wood. Good Is Not Nice: Despite being a hot-tempered jerk, Bram is working forJacob, and is opposed to the Man in Black. Hot-Blooded: He grows increasingly impatient outside the statue, and finally just charges in to his doom.

characters.name: Caesar
characters.description: A passenger aboard Ajira Airways Flight 316 from Los Angeles to Guam when it crashed on the Hydra Island. Caesar assumed a semi-leadership role among the small pocket of survivors there, and took an interest into exploring the DHARMA Initiative station on the island. Blown Across the Room: Ben blasts him away with a shotgun. Catchphrase: He likes calling people 'friend', especially when he's trying to take charge or threaten. Character Death: When Caesar attempts to stop the Man in Black and Ben from leaving Hydra Island, Ben shoots him in the chest with a shotgun. Horrible Judge of Character: Caesar is one of many people who end up worse off for putting any amount of trust in Ben.

characters.name: Principal Reynolds
characters.description: The principal of the Washington Tustin High School, at which Dr. Benjamin Linus and Leslie Arzt worked in the Flash-Sideways timeline and where John Locke also appeared as a substitute teacher. Reynolds seemed to have a chilly relationship with Dr. Linus, dismissing the importance of the "History Club" that Ben ran and forcing Ben to oversee afternoon detentions instead. The Bully: Reynolds pushes Ben around, dismissing him at every turn. Dirty Old Man: Reynolds, a middle-aged (and married) man, conducts an affair with the school nurse on school grounds, and in the nurse's own office, no less. Jerkass: He frequently belittles and insults Ben. He even threatens to destroy Alex's future academic career for something she had nothing to do with. Karma Houdini: He doesn't get much in the way of comeuppance for his adultery, bullying and abuse of power, save for having to give Alex a very positive letter of recommendation and acquiescing to Ben's request to hold the History Club at its old timeslot.

characters.name: Sarah
characters.description: Jack Shephard's ex-wife. They met when he performed emergency surgery on her after a car accident. Awful Wedded Life: Her marriage to Jack proves to be utterly miserable once the honeymoon stage is over; they cease communicating in any meaningful way and it's implied they have fundamental disagreements over whether or not to have children, since Sarah remarks on taking a pregnancy test which neither of them seem enthused about. The marriage is entirely cold and empty, with Jack flirting with infidelity and Sarah eventually leaving him for someone else before he even realises something's wrong. Babies Ever After: Her final appearance in "Through The Looking Glass" shows her as heavily pregnant, making it clear she's moved on since divorcing Jack. Florence Nightingale Effect: Jack saved Sarah from paralysis, and a mixture of her gratitude and his sense of responsibility to her results in them getting married. These foundations prove way too shaky to keep the marriage going once all the initial drama has passed. One Degree of Separation: The driver of the other car in her accident was Adam Rutherford, Shannon's father and Boone's stepfather.

characters.name: Marc Silverman
characters.description: Jack's best friend since childhood. On one occasion, Jack unsuccessfully attempted to defend him against schoolyard bullies and was also beaten. Childhood Friends: He's first seen as a child, getting the hell beat out of him by some bullies. Jack tries and fails to save him, but they remain solid enough friends that as adults, Marc is best man at Jack's wedding. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: It's a minor example, but despite being Jack's 'best friend' he isn't seen after his flashback appearance. Performance Anxiety: He has to get slightly drunk to perform his Best Man's Speech, but he does it for Jack."I'll be fine. After about 8 beers, I'll be fine."

characters.name: Kevin
characters.description: Sarah Shephard's fiancé at the time of her accident. Jack informed him of her accident, current condition, and subsequent paralysis. Kevin asked if they would still be able to make love but became distressed when Jack informed him that she may need professional care for the rest of her life. He stopped visiting and left her life not long afterwards. Disposable Fiancé: He only appears in one scene, and it's made very clear that he's not going to stick around for Sarah if it's an inconvenience to him. It's All About Me: He's concerned mostly with his needs, and how Sarah's accident affects him. He asks a few standard questions in a disinterested tone, then tries to find out whether she'll be able to have sex after the surgery. And when he hears she'll need professional care, he's out.Jack: There will be ongoing physical therapy, but if she works really hard -Kevin: Well, well, will we be able to, you know, make love?Jack: You need to know that there's a chance Sarah might very well need professional care for the rest of her life.Kevin: Like, she won't be able to go to the bathroom by herself?

characters.name: Sam
characters.description: The man who raised Kate, and whom she believed to be her biological father. Good Scars, Evil Scars: Despite his intimidating facial scars, Sam Austen is a good man at heart who loves his daughter dearly. I Want My Beloved to Be Happy: Sam loved Diane and accepted that Diane lovedWayne.Although a military man would make short work of a sleazy drunk, he wasn't going to interfere. He also didn't tell Kate the truth of her parentage because he feared she'd hurt Wayne.Kate: Why didn't you tell me that Wayne was my father? Why?Sam: I didn't tell you because I knew you'd kill him. And your mother loved him. The Mentor: As part of being aParental Substituteto Kate, he also taught her many of the skills that come in handy on the Island, like tracking. Mercy Lead: After Kate comes to see him for one last time, Sam agrees to wait an hour before calling the authorities.

characters.name: Tom
characters.description: Kate's childhood sweetheart. Many years later, he had a baby named Connor with his wife, Rachel. He became a doctor in St. Francis Hospital in Iowa, where he scheduled a fake MRI for Kate's mother, Diane Janssen, so that Kate could see her one last time before she dies. Character Death: He's shot and killed by a police officer while helping Kate escape. Childhood Friends: As a child, he was Kate's best friend. Happily Married: Tom is married with a son and seems pretty happy until Kate comes back. The Lost Lenore: He's Kate's long-lost love.

characters.name: Wayne
characters.description: Kate's biological father, though he was likely unaware of this. He beat Kate's mother, Diane, was an alcoholic, and made sexual advances toward Kate (which she vehemently rebuffed). He was killed by Kate when she blew up his house in 2001. Abusive Parents: Wayne supposedly never abused Kate physically, but he was still a sleazy drunk who beat her mother and leered after his daughter. The Alcoholic: When he returns home after a night spent drinking, Kate helps him into bed with the practice of someone who's done so many times before. Alcoholic Parent: To Kate. Asshole Victim: Only Diane mourns his death.

characters.name: Ray Mullen
characters.description: A farmer in Australia for whom Kate worked prior to the crash of Oceanic Flight 815. An Arm and a Leg: Ray is the first of many characters seen with a missing limb, in this case his right arm. Nice Guy: Despite his betrayal of Kate (which from an outsider's perspective, seems very reasonable due to her status as a dangerous fugitive), Ray is generally a nice man willing to give Kate room and board.

characters.name: Kevin Callis
characters.description: A Miami-Dade police officer who married Kate. They lived together for roughly six months. Disposable Fiancé: For Kate. She marries him, drugs him, dumps him and he's subsequently never seen again. Fair Cop: Kate certainly considers him to be one. Good Is Boring: He's a good man, but Kate quickly grows tired with the monotonous routine of being married to him. Happily Married: To Kate, or so he thought. She disabuses him of that notion when she drugs him.

characters.name: Mary & Warren Ford
characters.description: The mother and father of James "Sawyer" Ford. Warren killed Mary and himself after they were both conned by Anthony Cooper, who was working under the alias "Tom Sawyer." Mary engaged in adultery and facilitated their being robbed by Cooper, prompting Warren to kill her and then himself. Character Death: They both die in Warren'sMurder-Suicide. Deceased Parents Are the Best: Downplayed; Sawyer rarely speaks of them, but despite Mary cheating on Warren and Warren'sMurder-Suicide, Sawyer only blames Cooper for his parents' deaths and doesn't have a negative word to say about either of them beyond an idle comment that Warren "never got a chance" to beat him. Death by Origin Story: Their deaths essentially create Sawyer, leading him down the path of becoming aCon Man. Mama Bear: Mary's sole appearance has her desperately hiding her son from her furious, armed husband.

characters.name: Uncle Doug
characters.description: Sawyer's uncle. At his parents' funeral Doug finds him writing a letter and tells him that although he should want revenge on the man who did this, he should move on with his life and made him promise he wouldn't finish the letter. He says, "What's done is done." Ambiguously Related: It's not clear if he's Warren's brother (in which case, his surname would be Ford) or Mary's. Character Death: A brain tumor strikes him down off-screen. Convenient Terminal Illness: Doug dies from his aforementioned brain tumor, leaving Sawyer on his own. Nice Guy: Doug dissuaded Sawyer from pursuing vengeance, showing great sympathy to the boy and gently trying to guide him onto a better path.

characters.name: Hibbs
characters.description: A past associate of James "Sawyer" Ford, who worked with him on the Tampa Job. Hibbs provided Sawyer with the information that the real Sawyer was a man named Frank Duckett who was residing in Australia. Hibbs was lying, however, using Sawyer to kill Duckett because he owed Hibbs money. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Despite being played by a pretty big name in Sci-fi and having had quite an impact on Sawyer's life, he never appears again. Evil Counterpart: Hibbs is similar to Sawyer in many ways, having a manipulative side, a Southern accent, a penchant for nicknames (he calls Sawyer "Sawbucks"), a less-than-reputable lifestyle, and a rugged charm. However, Hibbs lacks any of Sawyer's redeeming qualities or his conscience; he plays Sawyer like a fiddle to get an innocent man murdered. Faux Affably Evil: He pretends that he's giving Sawyer information about the real Sawyer to make them even for a past job gone wrong, but he's actually tricking him into doing his dirty work. Karma Houdini: Hibbs gets away scot-free with his manipulation of Sawyer and indirect responsibility for the death of Frank Duckett.

characters.name: Frank Duckett
characters.description: An American running a shrimp stand in Australia. Sawyer was told by his associate Hibbs that Duckett was the original Sawyer. However, it turned out that Hibbs had tricked Sawyer, and Duckett merely owed Hibbs money, and because of this, Hibbs wanted Duckett dead, and thus Sawyer was conned into killing him. Just before he died, Duckett told Sawyer, "It'll come back around." Nice Guy: He was in a bad spot and owed money to the very shady Hibbs, but otherwise he seemed like a friendly, warm fellow. Posthumous Character: Sawyer kills him just before leaving Australia. Small Role, Big Impact: Frank's only onscreen for about three minutes total, but Sawyer's guilt over his death leads to the actions that put him on Flight 815 and cause the self-hatred that drives his character for the first three seasons.

characters.name: Gordy
characters.description: Sawyer's partner and Sawyer was indebted to him. He was having Sawyer perform a "long con" on Cassidy. He threatened to kill both Sawyer and Cassidy if he didn't go through with the con on her. Con Man: Like Sawyer, except he's more of a planner. He chooses the mark and does the research before Sawyer moves in. Faux Affably Evil: Gordy talks shop with Sawyer for a moment in a pretty casual tone but quickly resorts to threats. Fat Bastard: Part of the reason he's a planner is because he's an overweight schlubby guy. Jerkass: He's crass and uncouth, referring to Cassidy as a 'bitch'.

characters.name: Helen Norwood
characters.description: Locke's girlfriend for a period during his life before the plane crash, whom he had intended to marry. Bus Crash: She dies off-screen, after the actual crash of Oceanic 815. Character Death: Helen dies off-screen from a brain aneurysm. Deadpan Snarker: Part of what makes her such aFiery Redheadis her quick wit and dark sense of humor. She even jokes about Locke's missing kidney. Dropped a Bridge on Her: She sadly dies off-screen between seasons from a brain aneurysm.

characters.name: Emily Annabeth Locke
characters.description: The biological mother of John Locke. May–December Romance: With Cooper, who was apparently twice her age. Missing Mom: To Locke, whom she abandoned at birth. She comes back into his life just long enough to send him Cooper's way, then skips out on him again. Look Both Ways: During a fight with her mother, she runs onto the road without looking and gets hit by a car. Only in It for the Money: Emily only contacts Locke because she's being paid by Cooper to help with the con.

characters.name: Eddie Colburn
characters.description: An undercover police officer who befriended John Locke and infiltrated the commune which Locke had joined. Jerkass: Eddie is generally an unpleasant person; he has every reason to dislike the commune considering they're criminals, but he dismisses innocent-minded members like Locke as having daddy issues, treating them with scorn, and when Locke trains a gun on him he's smug and dismissive. The Mole: He's a cop going undercover to take down the commune. Perma-Stubble: His undercover look, it seems. Puppy-Dog Eyes: Has a great big pair of them.

characters.name: Jimmy Bane
characters.description: A criminal from whom Anthony Cooper stole $700,000 in a retirement con. Beard of Evil: He has a little goatee and is clearly a nasty fella. Evil Sounds Raspy: He has a low, gritty voice that fits with his shady appearance and even shadier deeds. Evil vs. Evil: He's an intimidating criminal who was cheated by and wants to get revenge on Anthony Cooper, a sociopathic con artist. Faux Affably Evil: It's clear he's a shady criminal, and his friendly overtones are laced with menace.

characters.name: Peter Talbot
characters.description: A young man who sought John Locke's help for his mother when she was wooed by a suave con man named "Adam Seward." He Knows Too Much: He was implicitly murdered by Anthony Cooper because of his investigation into Cooper's "Adam Seward" identity. Killed Offscreen: By Anthony Cooper. Locke only learns of his death from the detectives investigating the case, and it's never stated how he was killed. Posthumous Character: Cooper murders him long before the main timeline of the series. Properly Paranoid: Peter is very suspicious of his mother's fiance, and rightly so. Her fiance is Anthony Cooper, a seasoned con artist who has no qualms about adding murder to his list of crimes.

characters.name: GL- 12
characters.description: The man John played a war game with during his lunch break while working at the box company. Only Friend: He seems to be Locke's only friend at his work, and even in general. They play board games on their lunch break and have nicknames for each other. Only Known by Their Nickname: Locke only ever calls him 'GL-12'. His real name of Warren Goldberg is only mentioned in the script and credits.

characters.name: Frainey
characters.description: A private investigator hired by Locke to investigate his parents. Ignored Expert: He warns Locke about finding his father, having seen similar circumstances end badly many times before. He's completely right, but Locke doesn't listen."Here's the thing — your mother sought you out, so she's fair game. But this guy — maybe he doesn't even know you exist. I've done this enough times to know this stuff isn't meant to be, even though it may feel that way. But this probably won't have a happy ending. So, do you want it, or not?" Right for the Wrong Reasons: Frainey doesn't think that Locke seeking out his birth father will end well, doubting that Locke's father even knows that John exists. He's right that Locke meeting Cooper will come to a bad end, but it's because Cooper is well aware of Locke's existence, and is just using him to get a kidney (which turns out to just be thestartof Cooper's negative impact on John's life). Small Role, Big Impact: Frainey only appears in one scene in one episode, but he's the one who tracks down Anthony Cooper, allowing Locke to meet his biological father and setting off all the misery that follows.

characters.name: Mike & Jan
characters.description: The overseers of a self-sufficient commune. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: They're initially friendly and welcoming, talking about 'family' and the like. They show a much more unforgiving side when Eddie is revealed to be a cop.

characters.name: William Kincaid
characters.description: A physiotherapist based out of a California hospital. Nice Guy: Locke at least got blessed with an excellent carer. Kincaid is optimistic and determined to help John but never patronizes him.

characters.name: Gellert
characters.description: John Locke's science teacher at Cowin Heights High School. Stern Teacher: Gellert isn't the nicest guy in the world, but he does genuinely want to help Locke, even if the advice he gives is harsh.

characters.name: Omer
characters.description: Sayid's older brother. Abusive Parents: His father was a hard man, who believed thatA Real Man Is a Killer. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He seems nice enough, but he's really aDirty Cowardwho isn't above pressuring his own brother into trying to save his hide. Dirty Coward: Omer tries to get Sayid to clean up the messhemade, i.e. send his own brother into a confrontation with extremely dangerous criminals to save his own hide. He even tries to use his family as justification. Jerkass: He gets in over his head with dangerous people, and then tries to pressure Sayid into cleaning up his mess.

characters.name: Mr. Jarrah
characters.description: The father of Sayid and Omer, and he was a soldier in the Iraqi Republican Guard. Abusive Parent: To Sayid and Omer, with whom he was extremely harsh and domineering. He tried to instil very outdated values in them through emotional (and possibly physical) abuse. No Name Given: His actual name isn't given, although a casting call names him as "Hassan", which isn't canon. A Real Man Is a Killer: A fervent believer in this, as seen when he declares how proud he is of Sayid for killing a chicken that Omer could not.

characters.name: Cole & Hewitt
characters.description: Agents from the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) agent and Australian Secret Intelligence Service (ASIS), who blackmailed Sayid to work for them to betray his old friend Essam Tasir in order to find stolen explosives, all in exchange for information about Nadia's whereabouts. Good Is Not Nice: They're trying to foil a terrorism plot, but are doing so through shady means, specificallyBlackmail. Their personalities also leave a lot to be desired. Jerkass: Both of them come across as superior and smug. Jurisdiction Friction: Averted, they get along very well. Pet the Dog: They do this rather weakly with regard to Sayid. They're smug, amoral jerks but even they seem to realize how badly they screwed up and what they put Sayid through, showing evident shame at being partially responsible for Essam's death. When Sayid demands that they change his flight so he can claim Essam's body, they acquiesce without hesitation or question.

characters.name: Essam
characters.description: A former college roommate of Sayid at the University of Cairo, where he earned a degree in philosophy. Essam's wife, Zahra, was killed in the bombings of civilian areas in Baghdad (during the American invasion of Iraq), while shopping for a dress. In the events of his wife's death, the then angry and desperate Essam is lured into a terrorist cell in Sydney, Australia, that aims to disrupt the US-lead Coalition prison on Iraq. Ate His Gun: After Sayid's betrayal. Butt-Monkey: In his only episode, he's manipulated by terrorists following his wife's death and betrayed by his only friend. Despair Event Horizon: Following the death of his wife. Driven to Suicide: After Sayid reveals he's working with the CIA, Essam loses it and puts a gun in his mouth.

characters.name: Haddad
characters.description: The leader or a leading figure of the terrorist cell in Australia of which Essam was a member. What Happened to the Mouse?: It isn't clear what happened to him after Essam's suicide, although he was presumably arrested.

characters.name: Tariq
characters.description: Sayid's superior in the Republican Guard during Operation Desert Storm. When U.S. forces entered a bunker, he ordered the destruction of numerous documents. He was captured alongside Sayid. Asshole Victim: Tariq is a cowardly monster who kills civilians; it's easy to see why Sayid resorted to torturing him. Bad Boss: Aside from being aggressive toward his own men, when they're shredding documents and soldiers burst in with the command to stop or be shot, Tariq says nothing. He's willing to let them die for little reason. Cold-Blooded Torture: Sayid eventually resorts to torturing him for information. It works. Dirty Coward: Tariq easily orders Sayid to kill himself for the sake of his honor, but refuses to do the same thing because he values his own life above all else.Tariq: Take that bag. Put it over your head and tape it up. Kill yourself, now! That's an order. Do it and die with what little honor you have left.Sayid: You would have me take my own life — the information means nothing to you!

characters.name: Sami
characters.description: The husband of Amira, a woman who accused Sayid of torturing her once while he was working for the Republican Guard. Happily Married: To Amira. He adores and loves her, and goes so far as to kidnap, imprison and torture a man based solely on her word to achieve justice and closure for her. He has every intention of murdering Sayid, such is his depth of feeling for Amira. No-Holds-Barred Beatdown: He tortures Sayid with repeated, savage beatings fuelled by rage. Pay Evil unto Evil: Sami seemingly believes in this, brutally torturing Sayid as revenge for Sayid'sCold-Blooded Tortureof Amira. Undying Loyalty: To his beloved wife, Amira.

characters.name: Amira
characters.description: Sami's wife. When living in Iraq, Amira was tortured by Sayid while he was working for the Republican Guard. Her torture involved being scalded with hot oil, which left permanent scars on her arms and hands. Broken Bird: After her torture at the hands of Sayid, she became a recluse unable to leave her house. She was always afraid. Cold-Blooded Torture: She endured this at the hands of Sayid. Happily Married: To her husband, Sami, who's willing to kidnap, torture and possibly kill someone at her behest. Kind Hearted Cat Lover: What finally got her to leave her apartment was to stop a bunch of kids torturing a cat, which she then took in and cared for.

characters.name: Dave
characters.description: Hurley's imaginary friend, which he hallucinated while an inmate at the Santa Rosa Mental Health Institute. Hurley saw Dave again while on the Island, a setback in his battle against mental illness. Bald of Evil: He's as bald as Evan Handler, and while he isn't blatantly evil, he's aToxic Friend Influenceto Hurley. Deadpan Snarker: He's Hurley'sImaginary Friend, after all. Imaginary Friend: For Hurley, who doesn't realize it until he's shown evidence. After an incident with a deck collapse, Hurley imagined Dave while in the Mental Health Institute. Maybe Magic, Maybe Mundane: His appearance on-island is this both in-universe and out. The writers have conflicting reports over whether Dave was a genuine hallucination of Hurley or the Man in Black trying to off a candidate by encouraging him to commit suicide.

characters.name: Johnny
characters.description: A friend and co-worker of Hurley's at Mr. Cluck's. Deadpan Snarker: He's friends with Hurley, after all. Fair-Weather Friend:Inverted. When Hurley quits Mr. Cluck's, Johnny sticks by him and supports his decision. After finding out that Hurley quit because he'd won the lottery, Johnny becomes resentful and breaks off their friendship. We eventually learn that he and Starla ran off together, leaving Hurley behind. Fat and Skinny: He's the skinny to Hurley's fat.

characters.name: Starla
characters.description: An assistant at a music store Hurley frequently visited. Hurley was attracted to her for a long time but did not act on his feelings until the day after he won the lottery. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She seems like aNice Girlin her introduction, but it's later revealed she ran off with Johnny while dating Hurley.

characters.name: Lynn Karnoff
characters.description: A woman who posed as a fortune-teller to Hurley. Con Woman: Like pretty much all fortune tellers, she's just trying to con people out of money. Only in It for the Money: She rats out David Reyes pretty much instantly when Hurley offers her more cash to tell the truth. Phony Psychic: And paid by David to trick Hurley.

characters.name: Martha Toomey
characters.description: The widow of Sam Toomey. Agent Scully: Even after everything that's happened to her, she refuses to believe there's a curse associated with the Numbers.Martha:Curse? There's no curse.Hurley:But you just told me...Martha:You think I'd still have my leg if Sam hadn't picked the right number of beans?! You think that floods wouldn't have happened?! That homes wouldn't have burned down?! That people wouldn't have died?!Hurley:Well, yeah.Martha:You make your own luck, Mr. Reyes. Don't blame it on the damn numbers. You're looking for an excuse that doesn't exist. An Arm and a Leg: She lost her leg in a car accident.

characters.name: Jae Lee
characters.description: The wealthy son of the owner of the Seoul Gateway Hotel, and most likely would have gone on to manage and own the hotel himself someday had he not taken his own life. Character Death: Following Sun's rejection and Jin's beatdown and threats, Jae Lee kills himself. Driven to Suicide: After Jin beats him up and Sun leaves him, combined with a death threat from Mr. Paik, Jae Lee opts out of his problems by jumping from his apartment building. Nice Guy: Although Jae Lee initially appears stoic and serious, as soon as their respective parents leave, he breaks into a smile and puts Sun at ease by confessing that he finds the whole 'arranged' meeting just as outdated and awkward as she does. No-Holds-Barred Beatdown: Is on the receiving end of one from Jin.

characters.name: Mr Kwon
characters.description: Jin's father, a fisherman in his village. Good Parents: Probably the most shining example of a good parent in the entire series. He's humble, kind, forgiving, and raised Jin entirely on his own without even really knowing if he was the biological father. Mama's Baby, Papa's Maybe: He admits there's a possibility Jin's mother was lying about who Jin's biological father is, but it's clear he still loves Jin no matter what.

characters.name: White Suit
characters.description: One of Mr. Paik's henchmen. Person with the Clothing: Only known as 'White Suit'. Professional Killer: For Paik. Psycho for Hire: And Mr Paik has hired him.

characters.name: Hawaiian Shirt
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Pretends to just be an average guy. Cunning Linguist: An Anglophone American who delivers a warning to Jin in Korean. Faux Affably Evil: Seems like a friendly tourist, for all of two seconds. Person with the Clothing: Only known as 'Hawaiian Shirt'.

characters.name: Liam
characters.description: The lead singer of Drive Shaft, and Charlie's older brother. The Atoner: Liam feels terrible when he drops his infant daughter, and this incident spurs him on to ditch the heroin, get clean and leave his destructive lifestyle behind. Glory Hound: As the lead singer of the band, Liam basks in all of the attention that the band gets, even though Charlie is the one who actually writes the songs. Hookers and Blow: Much like Charlie, he indulges in this after getting some success with Driveshaft. I Am the Band: He response when Charlie tries to get him to disband Drive Shaft after his drug use gets out of control.

characters.name: Megan
characters.description: The wife of Simon Pace and the mother of Charlie and Liam Pace. She encouraged Charlie's musical inclinations; she told him that he was "special" and bought him a piano with hard-earned money. Dead Guy Junior: Karen names her and Liam's baby after her. Good Parents: Unlike Simon, Megan encouraged Charlie's musical dreams. Posthumous Character: She's long deceased by the time the series begins. In flashbacks, she's only ever seen when Charlie's a very young child. Missing Mom: Due to her death and all.

characters.name: Simon
characters.description: Husband to Megan Pace and the father of Charlie and Liam Pace. He worked as a butcher and vehemently disapproved of Charlie and Liam's musical careers. Fantasy-Forbidding Father: Simon didn't want his sons to be musicians, and from what little we see of him he wanted them to follow him in the family butcher business. Jerkass: As part of hisFantasy-Forbidding Fatherthing.Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Charlie does have some good memories of him, such as when he was teaching him to swim. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Charlie does have some good memories of him, such as when he was teaching him to swim. Posthumous Character: He's dead (the cause is unknown but likely to be fairly innocuous) by the time the series begins in earnest.

characters.name: Karen
characters.description: Liam Pace's wife, and mother of Liam's child, Megan.

characters.name: Francis Pryce Heatherton
characters.description: The owner of the Heatherton Corporation, and father to Lucy Heatherton. Former Teen Rebel: He was in a band as a teenager called 'The Protestant Reformation' which he's quite self-deprecating about. Honest Corporate Executive: He's a ridiculously good-natured chap who's also very rich. Nice Guy: Affable, good-humoured and an all-around genial fellow. Shout-Out: To "The Office". He brought a paper company in Slough, implied to be Wernham-Hogg.

characters.name: Lucy
characters.description: A young woman picked up by Charlie in hopes of getting money from her. She lived in Knightsbridge, England, the same area of London as Penelope. Her father, Francis Heatherton briefly employed Charlie at Heatherton Corporation and bought him a briefcase for his new job. Daddy's Girl: Lucy has a very good relationship with her beloved father. Missing Mom: Her father seems to be the only parent in her life. What the Hell, Hero?: Gives one to Charlie after he's discovered as a heroin addict and thief.

characters.name: Tommy
characters.description: Charlie's friend in London with with whom Charlie did heroin.

characters.name: Lily
characters.description: A heroin addict who spent the night with Charlie in Sydney, Australia, before he boarded Oceanic Flight 815. She pretended to be a big fan of Drive Shaft just so she could get her fix.

characters.name: Lindsey Littleton
characters.description: Claire's aunt, sister to Claire's mother Carole Littleton Jerk with a Heart of Gold: She's never seen getting along particularly well with anyone. Nevertheless, she did take Claire into her home and was very protective of her. Mama Bear: To Claire. She refuses to let Christian in, not wanting Claire to see her father as the pitiful drunk he truly is. Promotion to Parent: After a car accident sends her sister into a coma, Lindsey basically takes over as Claire's mother.

characters.name: Thomas
characters.description: Claire's ex-boyfriend and the biological father of Aaron. He lives in Australia and is an artist. The Baby Trap: Accuses Claire of lying about taking her birth control so she could do this to him, even though he was the one who talked her into keeping the baby when they first found out. Disappeared Dad: To Aaron, whom he abandons while Claire is still pregnant. Evil Counterpart: To Michael, funnily enough. Both were artists who got their girlfriends pregnant and didn't marry them. While Michael gave up his dreams and took construction work to provide for his family, staying loyal until his girlfriend pushed him away, Thomas ducks out and runs for the hills. It's All About Me: Thomas is far more concerned about his stupid 'art' than raising his child.Thomas:How in the hell am I supposed to be a dad, Claire? How about my painting, my life?

characters.name: Susan Porter
characters.description: A lawyer and Walt's mother. Amoral Attorney: We never see her in court as a lawyer, but she is an attorney, and she is most certainly amoral. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: At first glance, she seems blandly pleasant. However, she then proceeds to cheat on Michael with her boss, take a job in Australia without consulting the father of her son, blame Michael for this because he hasn't had any construction work lately despite being a lawyer herself, takes their son with her to live in Australia without sparing a single thought for Michael and does her utmost to cut him out of Walt's life by intercepting all his letters. To make matters worse, Michael gave up his artistic dream to support her and Walt while she went through law school. Character Death: Susan dies very suddenly from a blood disorder. Convenient Terminal Illness: She dies of a sudden illness, leaving Walt to suddenly have to go with Michael.

characters.name: Brian Porter
characters.description: Susan's boss, who was living and working as an attorney in Amsterdam in the Netherlands. Brian married Susan after her relationship with Michael ended. Amoral Attorney: Same as Susan: he's never seen in action, but he's certainly not a moral guy. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: The second Susan dies, Brian tries to cut Walt out of his life completely. He just leaves, and never sees Walt again, not even saying goodbye to the child he helped raised for nine years. It's All About Me: After Susan dies, Brian leaves his 10-year-old, just-bereaved stepson alone in Australia to pawn him off and never see him again. All he can think about is how hard Susan's death is for himself.Brian:I'm a wreck right now, okay. Don't you understand that?Michael:I'm supposed to give a damn about you?! Maternal Death? Blame the Child!: While not outright stated, his fear of Walt'sabilitiesseems to indicate he was suspicious that Walt was to blame for Susan's death.

characters.name: Sabrina Carlyle
characters.description: The mother of Boone, and the stepmother of Shannon. She cut Shannon off from the family fortune after the death of her husband Adam Rutherford, who died with a living trust rather than a will. She is also the owner of a wedding business, a subsidiary of which resulted in Boone moving away from New York to become the COO of her company. Abusive Mom: She's verbally and financially abusive toward Shannon. Evil Matriarch: Of the Carlyle-Rutherfords; she favors Boone and loved her husband, but she's mercilessly cold toward Shannon. Jerkass Has a Point: Sabrina does make a salient point about Shannon having fleeting interests, but it's clearly motivated by her own hatred of Shannon. Ice Queen: She wears a constant cold facial expression with icy eyes.

characters.name: Bryan
characters.description: Shannon's boyfriend in Australia. He helped her in a scheme to get money from Boone. Con Man: He and Shannon scammed Boone out of cash. He later took the money and left without cutting Shannon in. Greed: What prompted him to con Boone and later Shannon. Karma Houdini: He gets away scott-free, even after conning Boone and beating him up. No-Holds-Barred Beatdown: Inflicts one on Boone.

characters.name: Teresa Cortez
characters.description: The mother of Ana Lucia Cortez, and was also her boss at the Los Angeles Police Department. Da Chief: Of the LAPD. Good Parents: Even after a big argument and Ana Lucia running away, Teresa still comforts her when she calls and promises to be there when she lands. Iron Lady: She's very professional in her role as the LAPD chief. Mama Bear: To Ana Lucia, who she wants to protect and is eager to see JasonMcCormackput away for good.

characters.name: JasonMcCormack
characters.description: A criminal responsible for shooting Ana Lucia Cortez. Asshole Victim: He tried to kill a police officer using hollow points. But for Me, It Was Tuesday: Jason doesn't remember Ana's face when she confronts him. Character Death: Ana Lucia shoots him six times in revenge for his attempted murder of her. Karmic Death: Shot to death by the woman he shot.

characters.name: Yemi
characters.description: Eko's younger brother. Cain and Abel: Downplayed; he and Eko didn't want to kill each other, but they were certainly on opposing sides and came into conflict. Character Death: During a confrontation between the military and Eko's men on a runway, Yemi is shot in the chest. He dies immediately. Children Forced to Kill: Narrowly averted; a militia leader put a gun in a young Yemi's hand and ordered him to shoot a helpless old man, but when Yemi hesitated,Ekograbbed the gun and shot the old man himself. Dead Person Conversation: Yemi appears to Eko on the island, giving him instruction. Ultimately averted as it wasn't actually Yemi: It was the Man in Black masquerading as Yemi.Eko: I did not ask for the life that I was given. But it was given, nonetheless. And with it... I did my best."Yemi":You speak to me as if I were your brother.Eko: (Beat) Whoareyou?

characters.name: Goldie
characters.description: One of the Nigerian drug smugglers working with Eko and Olu. Accidental Hero: By kicking Eko out of the plane, he inadvertently saved Eko's life; the plane crashed on the Island, killing Goldie. Character Death: Goldie dies when his plane crash-lands on the island. Easily Forgiven: Despite the fact that he clearly intended to abandon Eko to the military and escape with the heroin himself, Eko doesn't hold a grudge against him; when he finds Goldie's body on the Island, he tells Charlie that Goldie saved his life. Only Known by Their Nickname: His real name is never revealed, he's merely 'Goldie' after his gold tooth.

characters.name: Amina
characters.description: A woman that works at the clinic. Her son, Daniel, was an altar boy at Yemi's church. Jerkass Has a Point: Ungrateful though she may be, Amina is right that, by killing Emeka and his men, Eko defiled Yemi's church with their blood, and she rightfully calls Eko out for planning to sell the vaccines himself. Oblivious Guilt Slinging: Against Eko, who has just seen his beloved brother die due partly to his actions.Amina:You remind me of [Yemi], you know. You're a good man, too. Ungrateful Bastard: Could be seen as this: Eko did kill Emeka, but she makes a valid point in stating that there will be another Emeka-type and Eko was going to sell the vaccine anyway.Eko:I see you have your vaccine.Amina:Do you expect me to be grateful? I know what you are planning to do.Eko:Those men! I helped—Amina:Those men will be replaced by other men. What the Hell, Hero?: Gives one to Eko for defiling the church and not giving in to Emeka."[Yemi's church] is no longer sacred! And one day you'll be judged for what you did! If I were you, I would start making my peace now. I would go to London and begin to repent. Because you owe God for every life you've taken. And you truly believe this is Yemi's? You owe him one church."

characters.name: Emeka
characters.description: A Nigerian gangster. He led the gang that threatened Yemi's village, telling Eko that if they did not give him 80% of the vaccine shipment (which he would sell for profit on the black market), he would no longer "offer them protection" from his own gang's violence. Asshole Victim: A violent militia leader who murdered innocents and got what he earned at the business-end of a machete. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: When Eko has him on his knees and is about to lay into him with a machete, Emeka begs in terror for his life. Bullying a Dragon: Emeka tries to intimidate and bully Eko, a vicious warlord posing as a priest. It works out for him about as well as it works out for everyone else who underestimated Eko. Character Death: Eko kills him with his own machete.

characters.name: Caldwell
characters.description: Eko's license forger who delivered him a false Australian passport with the name of "Oduduwa Ulu".

characters.name: Charlotte Malkin
characters.description: A young woman who supposedly drowned but came back to life. Maybe Magic, Maybe Mundane: Maybe she came back from the dead, maybe the undertaker was negligent. She certainly believes she came back from the dead, and even has a message for Eko from Yemi (whom Eko had never mentioned to her). Waking Up at the Morgue: She drowned and was believed dead after two hours in the water. The next day she woke up screaming during her autopsy.

characters.name: Joyce Malkin
characters.description: The wife of Richard Malkin and mother of Charlotte Malkin. According to her husband, she was a "zealot"; she called herself a devoted Catholic. The Fundamentalist: According to her husband, she's a religious 'zealot'.

characters.name: Emily Linus
characters.description: The wife of Roger and the mother of Ben. While in her seventh month of pregnancy with Ben, she and her husband were hiking through a forest outside of Portland when she went into premature labor. Roger delivered the child in the woods, but Emily suffered complications. Roger helped Emily and the baby to the side of a highway and flagged down Horace and Olivia Goodspeed for assistance. Before the Goodspeeds could drive the Linus family to the hospital, Emily died. Her dying words were a request that Roger name their son Benjamin. Character Death: Emily dies during childbirth. Dead Person Conversation: With Ben. She appears to him on the island, and talks to him. Death by Childbirth: Ben came early while she was on a hike with her husband, and she died just after his birth. Death by Origin Story: For Ben. She died shortly after giving birth to him.

characters.name: Rachel Carlson
characters.description: Baldness Means Sickness: She's bald because she's recovering from cancer. She later grows back all of her hair. Guinea Pig Family: Juliet's experimenting on her (with Rachel's consent) to try and get results. The Topic of Cancer: She's struggled with cancer for a good long time. What Happened to the Mouse?: Rachel is never seen again in the outside world apart from the video Ben shows Juliet, despite presumably having quite an interesting story to tell. Her sister disappeared without a trace working for a company that doesn't exist.

characters.name: Mr & Mrs Carlson
characters.description: Juliet and Rachel's parents. Amicably Divorced: They were heading toward one, considering how well they got along when breaking the news to Juliet and Rachel.

characters.name: Edmund Burke
characters.description: Juliet's ex-husband, and was also her boss when she worked at the Miami Central University Medical Research Laboratory‎. Asshole Victim: He was such an unrepentant asshole that it's more funny than anything when he gets his due. Bald of Evil: As per usual forŽeljko Ivanek; Burke is bald and as amoral as they come. Blackmail: Ed threatens Juliet in a subtle way, raising the issue of her research's possible 'criminal concerns'. The Bully: He treats Juliet like a doormat, lording his new young girlfriend over her.

characters.name: Sherry
characters.description: A young woman who was involved romantically with Juliet's former husband, Edmund Burke prior to Juliet's arrival on the island. She was hired as a research assistant by Burke for his lab, Miami Central University Medical Research Laboratory, where she worked alongside Juliet. May–December Romance: With Edmund. Sexy Research Assistant: To Edmund Burke.

characters.name: Isabella
characters.description: The wife of Richard Alpert. Character Death: Isabella dies of tuburclosis long before the events of the series begin. Dead Person Conversation: With Richard, on the island. Her conversation with him (relayed by Hurley) is what gives Richard the strength needed to help the survivors. Dying Alone: She dies while Richard is out trying to find a cure. Ethereal White Dress: Only ever seen in white, to symbolize herpurity and goodness— and also her illness andPosthumous Characterstatus.

characters.name: Father Suarez
characters.description: A Catholic priest at a prison in Tenerife, Canary Islands. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Suarez seems nice enough, bringing Richard food and getting ready to take his confession. Then he shows his true colours. Corrupt Church: He's as corrupt as they come, taking advantage of his standing in the church and influence on others to make himself some cash in the slave trade. Greed: He condemns prisoners to a lifetime of slavery just for a few pieces of silver. Hate Sink: There is nothing remotely likable about him. He is cruel, smug, condescending, and self-righteous, all of which is thinly masked byan insincere aura of fatherly compassion.

characters.name: Jonas Whitfield
characters.description: An officer on the Black Rock, a ship owned by Magnus Hanso. In 1867, the Black Rock docked in Tenerife, Canary Islands, where Jonas bought a number of men to serve as slaves, among them Ignacio and Ricardo. The Alcoholic: It's pretty clear from his disheveled state that he has a drinking problem. On the commentary for his episode, even the actors and writers point it out. Asshole Victim: It's hard to feel sorry for a slaver who murders his 'property' when the going gets tough. Character Death: The Smoke Monster bursts through the Black Rock, grabs Whitfield, and lifts him off to his certain death. Evil Brit: If being involved in the slade trade wasn't enough, his evil is proven by his murder of the surviving slaves.

characters.name: Ignacio
characters.description: A slave aboard the Black Rock, a ship owned by Magnus Hanso. In 1867 while chained inside the ship, he met and befriended Ricardo, a fellow slave. When the ship was hit by a storm, Ignacio saw land nearby, an Island, and as the ship came closer, he saw an enormous statue and screamed that it was the Devil. Butt-Monkey: He's a slave on a crashed ship who's killed by his 'owner'. He does not have much luck. Impaled with Extreme Prejudice: By Jonas Whitfield with a sword. Nervous Wreck: As would you be, trapped on an island with your jailors. Posthumous Character: Died hundreds of years prior to the plane crash.

characters.name: Brother Campbell
characters.description: The leader of the Eddington Monastery in Scotland. Aborted Arc: He's seen in a picture with Eloise Hawking, but this is never explained or explored.
